title: Anthropic’s Annualized Revenue Tops $65B Before IPO
summary: Bloomberg's Anthony Hughes joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Anthropic is on track to generate annualized revenue of more than $65 billion based on its current performance, according to people familiar with the matter, up more than sevenfold from its pace at the end of last year. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Dollar Tumbles to Weakest in Three Months on Treasury Buyback
summary: The dollar tumbled by the most in three weeks after the Trump administration’s unexpected bond buyback announcement reversed a Treasury market rout that had pushed long-dated yields to the highest since 2007.

title: Shein Is Said to Target Up to $27B Valuation in HK IPO
summary: Bloomberg's Norah Mulinda joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Fast-fashion retailer Shein is targeting a valuation in the range of $26 billion to $27 billion in its initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter, a sharp drop from its peak value. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Guggenheim’s Beaten-Down Loan Whipsaws as Lenders Digest Call
summary: A loan issued by the financing entity of Guggenheim Investments whipsawed on Wednesday after executives reiterated to lenders that earnings would likely improve in the third quarter while steering clear of details about the wide-ranging probe into Mark Walter’s business empire.

title: Goldman Strikes Deal to Buy LCN to Become Hands-Off Landlord
summary: Bloomberg's Katherine Chiglinsky joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Goldman Sachs struck its second deal in a week as the firm pushes ahead with plans to grow its $4 trillion money-management arm. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Carvana Up as Report on Walter’s Pledged Stake Allays Fear
summary: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. recovered some losses from a two-day selloff, after a report showed billionaire Mark Walter’s stake in the company was pledged, meaning he wouldn’t be able to immediately sell it as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.

title: Mark Walter Dangled Guggenheim Stake to Secure Loans
summary: Bloomberg's Sridhar Natarajan joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Mark Walter offered to pledge his stake in his prized financial assets as part of a broader effort to raise billions of dollars in quick order. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Climb as Treasury Steps In to Support Bonds: Markets Wrap
summary: Wall Street staged a rebound after the Treasury said it plans to boost buybacks of longer-dated bonds, a signal the US wants to lower borrowing costs after yields hit multi-decade highs.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
summary: Oil rose to the highest in more than three weeks, as US refiners ramped up crude consumption and a spat between the United Arab Emirates and Iran heightened regional tensions.

title: Operation Twist Redux: Bessent Moves Evoke Crisis-Fighting Fed
summary: The Trump administration’s surprise move to ramp up buybacks of long-dated Treasuries is drawing parallels with the Federal Reserve’s “Operation Twist,” a strategy that was last deployed in 2011 to pull down bond yields.

title: Gold Surges as Treasury Buyback Plan Sends US Yields Lower
summary: Gold rallied to the highest since early June as US government bond yields fell following the Treasury’s surprise liquidity injection, providing a tailwind for the precious metal.

title: Fed Minutes Show Many Officials Wanted Rate Hike in July
summary: Several Federal Reserve officials favored an interest-rate hike last month and many indicated that policy tightening would be necessary if inflation didn’t decline, a record of the central bank’s most recent policy debate showed. The next Fed decision comes in September. Bloomberg's Michael McKee reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Goldman Gauges Demand for CoreWeave-Tied Data Center Bond
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is sounding out investor interest on a junk bond to fund construction of a data center leased to CoreWeave Inc., adding to a wave of borrowing tied to the neocloud firm as it seeks to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom.

title: Copper Traders Rush Metal Into LME Warehouses to Ease Squeeze
summary: A historic squeeze on the copper market eased somewhat after large inflows of readily available metal into the London Metal Exchange, although signs of underlying physical tightness remain.

title: TrueCar CEO Sees Auto-Industry Peril as Tariff Threat Sows Doubt
summary: TrueCar Inc. Chief Executive Officer Scott Painter warned that US-Canada trade uncertainty poses a greater threat to the auto industry than tariffs themselves because it upends manufacturers’ decision-making ability.

title: Iran Has 'Little Incentive' To Open Strait, Says Former Ambassador Daniel Fried
summary:
Daniel Fried, former US ambassador to Poland, said 'Iranians have little incentive in the near term' to allow the Strait of Hormuz to open and that a solution to the conflict will require patience. Fried, who also served as the assistant Secretary of State for Europe, also said that when it comes to assisting Ukraine in war against Russia, the US is leaving 'perfectly good leverage on the table' because Ukrainian success also means success for the US. 
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stripe Agrees to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter; No Terms Disclosed
summary: Stripe Inc. has agreed to buy OpenRouter Inc., adding one of the fastest-growing gateways to artificial intelligence models as the payments giant pushes deeper into the infrastructure powering the AI boom. Terms weren’t disclosed.

title: ‘The Treasury Is Watching’: Bessent’s Buybacks Jolt Bonds
summary: A surprise US Treasury announcement on Wednesday is the most concrete evidence yet that the recent selloff in long-dated debt is concerning to Secretary Scott Bessent.

title: Treasury’s Potentially Limitless Buybacks Cloud T-Bill Outlook
summary: The US Treasury Department’s decision to boost buybacks of long-dated bonds is complicating the outlook for issuance of short-term securities, including Treasury bills, which are expected to be used to finance the plan.

title: Betterment CEO Warns on Sports Betting
summary: Betterment CEO Sarah Levy sounds the alarm on Gen Z treating sports betting like investing. She joins Open Interest to explain why gambling apps, social-media financial advice and speculative trading are blurring the line between entertainment and long-term wealth building—and why investors need stronger guardrails. (Source: Bloomberg)
